label: How much each species can suffer, relative to a chicken (Rethink Priorities)

rows.label: A chicken's capacity to suffer, relative to a chicken

source.title: Rethink Priorities, welfare range estimates (Fischer et al. 2023)

rows.explainer: The chicken is the reference animal, so its own weight here is 1. How a chicken's suffering compares with a person's (Rethink Priorities' median, 33%) is not here: it is the one animal slider, "A chicken's suffering vs a person's", so the chicken's uncertainty lives in one place.

rows.label: A pig's capacity to suffer, relative to a chicken

source.title: Rethink Priorities, welfare range estimates (Fischer et al. 2023)

rows.explainer: Rethink Priorities' median welfare range for pigs (0.515 of a person's) divided by the chicken's (0.332). The range is pigs' 5th and 95th percentiles divided by the chicken's median. Rethink's figures already allow for the chance an animal isn't sentient, so nothing is multiplied in again.

rows.label: A cow's capacity to suffer, relative to a chicken (stand-in: pig)

source.title: Rethink Priorities, welfare range estimates (Fischer et al. 2023): pigs, used for cattle

rows.explainer: Rethink Priorities didn't estimate cattle. Our stand-in is the pig, the closest farmed mammal they did estimate. A judgment, not their figure.

rows.label: A farmed fish's capacity to suffer, relative to a chicken (mean of carp and salmon)

source.title: Rethink Priorities, welfare range estimates (Fischer et al. 2023): carp and salmon
source.quote: Carp: median 0.089, 0–0.568; salmon: median 0.056, 0–0.513; chickens: median 0.332

rows.explainer:
Rethink Priorities estimated two farmed fish, carp (0.089 of a person's) and salmon (0.056). We use their mean, 0.0725, divided by the chicken's 0.332, for farmed and wild-caught fish alike. The high end is the mean of their 95th percentiles over the chicken's median.

Low end: Rethink's table rounds both 5th percentiles to 0. We use 0.0005 (half the table's last digit) so ranges stay finite; ours, not theirs.

rows.label: A shrimp's capacity to suffer, relative to a chicken

source.title: Rethink Priorities, welfare range estimates (Fischer et al. 2023)

rows.explainer:
Rethink Priorities' median welfare range for shrimp (0.031 of a person's) divided by the chicken's (0.332): about a tenth of a chicken. The range is very wide: the 95th percentile is more than three chickens.

Low end: Rethink's table rounds the 5th percentile to 0. We use 0.0005 (half the table's last digit) so ranges stay finite; ours, not theirs.

rows.label: A wild bird's, mammal's or amphibian's capacity to suffer, relative to a chicken (stand-in: chicken)

source.title: Rethink Priorities, welfare range estimates (Fischer et al. 2023): chickens, with fish and pigs as the range

rows.explainer: For wild vertebrates other than fish (small birds, rodents, frogs), which Rethink Priorities didn't estimate, our stand-in is the chicken. The range runs from farmed fish to the pig. A judgment, not their figure.

rows.label: An insect's capacity to suffer, relative to a chicken (black soldier fly)

source.title: Rethink Priorities, welfare range estimates (Fischer et al. 2023): black soldier fly, silkworm, bee
source.quote: Black soldier fly: median 0.013; silkworm: median 0.002; bee: median 0.071; chickens: median 0.332

rows.explainer: For insects in general (mostly wild ones), our stand-in is the black soldier fly (0.013 of a person's, over the chicken's 0.332). The range runs from the silkworm's median (0.002) to the bee's (0.071), the lowest and highest insects Rethink Priorities estimated. A judgment, not their figure.
